source.label: Recovering sums from a mean square over rows written as a power part times a primitive part: an inequality for all primitive parts at once, a two-sided form under a sieve for primitive rows, and the family of heights as the case without recurrence

reviewer: Claude Code proof assessment; fresh medium reviewer

claims.summary: R a finite set of rows, each a pair (v, w); complex numbers A_(v,w); M = sum over R of |A_(v,w)|^2. (1) If for each w in a set W0 there are a number A^(w), a set P_w of v with (v, w) in R, and E_w >= 0 with |A_(v,w) - A^(w)| <= E_w for v in P_w, then sum over w in W0 of |P_w| (|A^(w)| - E_w)_+^2 <= M. (2) If 1 denotes one value of w, B_v = A_(v,1) for v in V = {v : (v,1) in R}, and for each v in V the rows (v, w) with w != 1 have sum of |A_(v,w)|^2 at most S_v, rows with v outside V being absent, then sum over V of |B_v|^2 <= M <= sum over V of |B_v|^2 + sum over V of S_v; and if |B_v - A| <= E on V then |V| (|A| - E)_+^2 <= M <= 2 |V| (|A|^2 + E^2) + sum of S_v. (3) Exponents: with D >= 2, H = D^beta, k >= 1, |P_w| >= c (H/N(w))^(1/k) for the w in W0, all of norm N(w) <= D^gamma, and M <= C D^(1+eps) H, part (1) gives sum over W0 of (|A^(w)| - E_w)_+^2 <= (C/c) D^(1 + eps + beta - (beta - gamma)/k), so for |W0| >= c' D^gamma a mean value at most (C/(c c')) D^(1 + eps + (beta - gamma)(1 - 1/k)); with S_v = C D^(1+eps)(H N(v)^(-k) + D) the upper bound of (2) is 2|V|(|A|^2 + E^2) + C D^(1+eps)(H sum N(v)^(-k) + D |V|). (4) Heights: for complex a_n, D < n <= 2D, A(t) = sum a_n n^(-it), S = sum |a_n| and 0 < E: |A(t) - A(0)| <= E for |t| <= delta = E/(S log(2D)); so if the integral of |A|^2 over [-T, T], T >= delta, is at most B, then |A(0)| <= (B S log(2D)/(2E))^(1/2) + E; with |a_n| = 1 for all D values of n and B >= D^2 this bound is at least 0.83 D for every E.
claims.assessment: Working elementary proof: positivity of the terms of a mean square, grouped by primitive part in (1) and by power part in (2); (3) is arithmetic of exponents; (4) is the mean value inequality for a function that moves by at most E on an interval. Bookkeeping: part (1) is the moment extraction exponents at the second moment summed over disjoint primitive parts, and part (2) adds a triangle inequality; registered as context for the reading it supports. For the imported family (rows u = v^6 w) nothing is verified: the instantiation assumes the import's mean square over all rows as read in an earlier entry, the count of v, and the recurrence defect; the sieve hypothesis of (2) is not known to me for sextic symbols.
claims.rationale: Answers the fourteenth route review's two questions on the imported device. As the family's order falls the number of recurring rows and the defect improve; the hypothesis, the mean square over all rows, is by the lower side of (2) at least the mean square on the power rows, which for coefficients one exceeds the claimed strength whenever beta < k/(k-1), the range in which the extraction's exponent is below one (counts of primes stated, not derived); so at every order the mean square must use the particular coefficients. A sieve of large-sieve strength for primitive rows gives the mean square from the bound on the power rows when the rows number at least D^(k/(k-1)); below that this upper bound does not suffice, which shows nothing about what is true. In the family of heights the recurrence proved is on an interval of length E/(S log 2D) and the extraction gives nothing from it; recurrence at other heights is not examined. Part (1) shows the import's mean square, if true, bounds on average the twists of norm up to D^gamma; with the defect bounded trivially this says something only for beta - gamma >= 6/7, and it is of interest only for gamma <= 1.

relationships: Part (1) with a single primitive part is that proposition at the second moment; that proposition also treats higher moments, which this one does not, so neither implies the other.
